bullets.title: THE ROTATION HELD FOR A SECOND SESSION AND WIDENED INTO A NAMED TRADE — CROWDSTRIKE CLOSED AT A RECORD, PALO ALTO +13%, WHILE MARVELL AND NVIDIA KEPT FALLING
bullets.summary: Archive grep on Palo Alto, Zscaler, Fortinet, Marvell: zero hits; CrowdStrike one unrelated hit (8 Sep). Tuesday's tape: CrowdStrike +13.85% to a record close, Palo Alto Networks +13.09%, Fortinet +9.04%, Zscaler +8.4%, against Marvell -7.4% and Nvidia -2.8%, with SPY -0.45% — the index went nowhere while capital moved within it. Stated catalyst unchanged from Monday: Amodei's pacing essay, read by desks as raising expected enterprise spend on vulnerability management and systemic cyber risk.
bullets.how: YES — it upgrades yesterday's finding from an event to a trend. The second fire recorded Monday as the first time PRAGMA's thesis was priced rather than argued, and was careful to call one session a signal rather than proof. Two consecutive sessions, with a record close in the control layer and continued selling in the capability layer, is a position being taken. The buyer-facing use should stay narrow: not evidence that AAIR scores are valuable, but evidence that the market now distinguishes the layer that builds capability from the layer that governs it — the premise PRAGMA has had to establish from scratch in every conversation. Logged caution: a two-day rotation driven by one essay is a sentiment trade, and sentiment trades unwind. The durable read is the distinction being drawn, not the percentages.

bullets.title: THE REPORT HAS NEVER ONCE CARRIED A MACRO CALENDAR ITEM, AND THE ONE LANDING TOMORROW AT 14:00 ET IS THE FIRST FED RATE HIKE SINCE 2023
bullets.summary: Archive grep on FOMC, Federal Reserve, rate hike, basis point, interest rate: zero hits across the entire archive, all eighty days of it. The FOMC meets 15-16 September; the decision and Summary of Economic Projections land Wednesday 16 September at 14:00 ET; market-implied probability of a +25bp hike is ~91%; current target range 3.5-3.75%; futures priced at Monday's close carry it to ~4.2% by December and ~4.6% by September 2027. The same coverage names higher-than-expected rates — not only the pacing essay — as a driver of the chip drawdown.
bullets.how: YES, and the more important of today's two tape findings. The second fire's lesson was 'watch the tape.' A tape is a consequence; a calendar is a cause — and this report maintains a DATED DEADLINES list carrying Sonar retirement, Docusign GA and a client-cert cutoff that has never contained a macro date. That is a real hole for an ecosystem whose competitive premise is about where capital goes: the discount rate is the input to every AI-capex thesis on the list, to every agent-platform raise tracked here, and to the timing of Anthropic's own IPO. Concretely: if the hike lands as priced, the rotate-out-of-compute trade in bullet 1 gains a second unrelated engine and the two become hard to separate — exactly the confound a report that started watching prices yesterday will mis-attribute. Add the FOMC calendar to DATED DEADLINES permanently.

bullets.title: THE CLAIM-GREP WORKED ON ITS FIRST OUTING AND KILLED TWO CANDIDATES — INCLUDING THE IDENTICAL URL THIS REPORT PUBLISHED ON ITS FIRST DAY. SIXTH AND SEVENTH STALE PACKAGE IN FOUR DAYS
bullets.summary: (i) The search layer returned 'TikTok launches MCP server to let AI agents run campaigns' as 14 September news. Archive grep on TikTok: five hits, earliest 2026-06-29, whose bullet 1 is the same Digiday URL and correctly dated the launch to TikTok World in May 2026, with Agentic Hub following 30 June; our 27 Aug entry already wrote the thread's closing line. Killed on prior coverage, not dateline — there is no new dateline. (ii) The search layer also returned Anthropic's confidential S-1 as a September item. It is 1 June 2026; archive grep on S-1 hits 30 Jun, 6 Jul, 12 Jul, 13 Jul and 13 Sep. Killed.
bullets.how: YES. First: the method fix written four hours ago caught both candidates in its first hour, and neither would have been caught by the older item-grep alone — the TikTok item would have passed a naive 'is this URL new' test only because nobody would think to check a URL the search layer presented with a fresh date. Second, less comfortable: six mis-attributed packages in three days became seven and eight today, all from the same retrieval layer. That is a degraded input, not bad luck. The report's defence is a grep run by hand on every candidate; the correct fix is to stop treating the search layer's date as a date and require a dateline read at the page — which the second fire already did for ImagineArt and which should now be the rule, not the exception.

bullets.title: 2.1.271 IS NOW CORROBORATED AT THE VENDOR'S OWN REPOSITORY, AND 2.1.272 SHIPPED AT 00:42 UTC TODAY WITH NOTHING IN IT FOR US
bullets.summary: Archive grep on 2.1.272: zero hits, new. The second fire closed the 2.1.271 question at a third-party changelog-tracking repo after code.claude.com proved unreachable and the Releasebot mirror proved stale. Both release tags now resolve at anthropics/claude-code itself, so the morning fire's claim is confirmed at the vendor rather than at a mirror of a mirror. 2.1.272 is a maintenance release — CLI bug fixes, crash reduction, stability for common workflows — with no new configuration surface.
bullets.how: YES, with the emphasis deliberately inverted. The newsworthy half is that a two-day provenance chase closed cleanly at the primary. The useful half is that today's actual release contains nothing, which means omitClaudeMd from 2.1.271 is still the one-line change sitting unexecuted, exactly as it was this morning. Three fires in one day have each named it. A flag that costs one frontmatter line and stops a ~130-file corpus loading into every subagent has survived three separate write-ups without being typed into a file — a fact about us, not about the changelog.

bullets.title: STANDING ACTIONS — DAY FIFTEEN, THIRD FIRE. THE LIST GAINS ITS FIRST MACRO DEADLINE AND LOSES NOTHING
bullets.summary: NEW DATED DEADLINE, MACRO, FIRST OF ITS KIND: FOMC decision + dot plot, Wednesday 16 September 14:00 ET, ~91% implied for +25bp from 3.5-3.75%. CONFIG (unwritten): maxEffortLevel; --system-prompt-snapshot off; CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS still default; per-command allowed_domains; omitClaudeMd — named in all three fires today, still untyped; (b) the four Entra MCP controls, TWELFTH asking, five lines. ARTIFACT: (a) incident log, six rows still prose; (c) skill-corpus audit — three instruments, zero runs, third fire of the same day; (f) standardize on ONE creative-ops MCP behind graphic-designer — 63 days, unblocked as of the second fire, unmoved. READ: RFC 9449, RFC 8707, body of arXiv 2609.00006. CARRIED: OPENROUTER_MODEL=deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash (provider rerouted 04:00 UTC 14 Sep, still unread); which dsh / ls ~/.dsh; the launchd seam. DEADLINES: FOMC 16 Sep (tomorrow), Sonar 27 Sep, Docusign MCP GA 30 Sep, client-cert 17 Nov, DCR removal after summer 2027. KILLED ON PRIOR COVERAGE: TikTok Ads MCP; Anthropic confidential S-1; arXiv 2603.09619 (twenty-one prior hits) and 2602.05447. KILLED ON DATELINE: Sakana AI's Fugu Ultra v2.0 (11 Sep) — zero archive hits, so new to us, but four days stale with no agent surface. EMPTY, REPORTED EMPTY: frontier models — nothing dated 14-15 Sep; funding thin rather than empty — Highstock $30M Series A (a16z), UrgentIQ $15M (Five Elms), Pave Finance $15M, all 14 Sep, none agent-platform; arXiv — nothing newer than 2609.10132 (9 Sep), fourth consecutive fire empty.
bullets.how: YES — the list's composition is the finding: everything added today was added by an outside calendar, and nothing on it was closed by us.

praxis_lesson: BOTH METHOD FIXES FROM THIS AFTERNOON WORKED ON THEIR FIRST OUTING — AND WHAT THEY REVEALED IS THAT THE PROBLEM IS UPSTREAM OF OUR JUDGEMENT. The claim-grep caught two candidates in its first hour, one of which was the identical Digiday URL this report published on day one, re-served with a September date. That is now the seventh and eighth mis-attributed package in three days from the same retrieval layer. A hand-run grep on every candidate is a good defence and also the wrong shape of fix, because it scales with our discipline rather than with the problem. The rule that actually holds is the one the second fire used on ImagineArt without generalising it: never accept the search layer's date as a date — read the dateline at the page, every time, or kill the item. Elevate that from a thing we did once to the standing intake rule. SECOND, AND IT IS THE DAY'S REAL FINDING: WE ADDED 'WATCH THE TAPE' YESTERDAY AND DISCOVERED WITHIN ONE FIRE THAT A TAPE IS A CONSEQUENCE. Tuesday confirmed Monday — CrowdStrike to a record close, Palo Alto +13%, chips still falling — a better citation than any changelog for the claim that the market now prices the control layer separately from the capability layer. But the cause of tomorrow's move is already on a public calendar: the Fed is expected, at 91%, to raise rates for the first time since 2023, at 14:00 ET on 16 September. This report has run for eighty days with a DATED DEADLINES list and has never contained a single macro date — zero archive hits on FOMC, Federal Reserve, rate hike, basis point or interest rate. An ecosystem whose entire thesis is about where capital goes has been reading vendor blogs and not the calendar that sets the discount rate on all of it. Worse: if the hike lands as priced, the rotation in bullet 1 acquires a second engine and the two become confounded, so a report that started watching prices yesterday is about to mis-attribute its own best finding. THIRD, THE ONE THAT SHOULD STOP BEING WRITTEN AND START BEING DONE: omitClaudeMd has now been named as the actionable item in the morning fire, the second fire, and this one. Three write-ups, one frontmatter line, zero edits. Standing action (f) is at 63 days with its blocker removed. (b) is at its twelfth asking for five lines of config. Today produced three fires, fourteen bullets and two method upgrades, and moved exactly zero items off the standing list — while the provider rerouted our model, the Fed scheduled our discount rate, and the market repriced our thesis. Everything that changed today was changed by somebody else, for the third consecutive fire.
